naming_finding.observed_role: MSVC scalar deleting destructor wrapper: call the complete destructor, release `this` when bit 0 of a callee-cleaned dword flag is set, return `this`.
naming_finding.consequence: Ghidra's vftable label PTR_App__IMessageManager__Get_01401798 is derived FROM this mislabel and inherits it; the vftable is real, the name attached to it is not corroborated.

observed_original_abi.return_type: void* -- MOV EAX,ESI at 0x0067dc98 materialises the receiver into the return register
observed_original_abi.note: The Ghidra decompilation reports "return in_ECX" and "WARNING: Unknown calling convention". That is a decompiler artifact: the disassembly has an explicit MOV EAX,ESI immediately before POP ESI/RET. The disassembly is authoritative here.

observed_mechanics: PUSH ESI; MOV ESI,ECX at 0x0067dc80-0x0067dc81 spill the receiver into ESI; ECX is left intact so the following call is still thiscall on the same object.
CALL 0x0067db10 at 0x0067dc83 runs unconditionally, before the flag is even read. It is the complete-object destructor.
TEST byte [ESP+8],0x1 at 0x0067dc88 reads the flag, not [ESP+4]: the preceding CALL has pushed a return address, so the frame is saved-ESI, return address, flag.
Only bit 0 of the flag is examined. The remaining 31 bits are ignored by this body.
When bit 0 is set, PUSH ESI; CALL 0x00f47380; ADD ESP,4 at 0x0067dc8f-0x0067dc95 releases the receiver. The ADD ESP,4 makes 0x00f47380 a __cdecl callee-cleaned by the caller.
MOV EAX,ESI at 0x0067dc98 runs on both paths, so the receiver is returned whether or not the release happened.
There is no null check on the receiver in this body; 0x00f47380 is the only null guard, and it guards its argument inside its own body.

validation.build_result: clean, no diagnostics, under both compilers at every optimisation level tried
validation.syntax_result: -fsyntax-only with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic is clean under clang++; under g++ it emits three -Wattributes notes ('thiscall attribute is used for non-class method') for the thiscall port typedef, the entry-point prototype and the entry-point definition. Those notes are inherent to modelling an MSVC thiscall member function reached through a C linkage, are not in the -Wall -Wextra -Werror set the gate uses, and were not silenced.
validation.model_test_result: exit code 0 under both compilers at -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3/-Os
validation.generated_body_evidence: with -fno-pic -no-pie the emitted sequence is 56 / 89 ce / e8 .. / f6 44 24 08 01 / 74 09 / 56 / e8 .. / 83 c4 04 / 89 f0 / 5e / c2 04 00 -- instruction for instruction the original 30 bytes 56 8b f1 e8 88 fe ff ff f6 44 24 08 01 74 09 56 e8 eb 96 8c 00 83 c4 04 8b c6 5e c2 04 00. Two encodings differ for free because both spell the same instruction (the original writes the register moves as 8b f1 / 8b c6, mov r32,r/m32, where the assembler picks 89 ce / 89 f0, mov r/m32,r32) and the two call displacements address the local shims. Under a default position-independent build both compilers prepend a nine-byte __x86.get_pc_thunk.ax PC anchor, which is a toolchain artifact and not part of the reconstruction.

static_validation_blockers.why: The machine-derived receiver record names no register -- register=null, reason=ecx_read_without_deref, because this 11-instruction body reads ECX and never dereferences it -- so there is no receiver window to ground a declared offset against. The register-agnostic absence arm is excluded in turn: the complete listing DOES address memory, at TEST byte ptr [ESP + 0x8], which is the stack argument slot and not a receiver field. The check therefore has nothing to say in either direction.
static_validation_blockers.not_a_source_defect: The only way to move this check off NOT_AVAILABLE from the source side would be to declare a field offset in the span, which would be a claim this body demonstrably does not make. It was deliberately not done.

static_validation_blockers.why: The derived ABI record abstained: conventions.calling_convention is null, confidence UNKNOWN, abstained_because 'receiver_not_determinable: ecx_read_without_deref'. The persisted record's claim (__thiscall, callee stack cleanup) and the source's declaration agree -- there is no conflict, so this is not a FAIL -- but the derived oracle is not proven, so the check warns. The source cannot raise this to PASS without contradicting the abstention.
